# Responsive Windows for Workgroups 3.11

> An OS-as-website. Windows for Workgroups 3.11, emulated in the browser and rearranged so it
> can be browsed across desktop, tablet and mobile. By Joshua Gross (https://gross.is).
> Live at https://win31.gross.is/

## What it is

An operating system in the shape of a website. The question it was built to answer: how close can
Windows 3.1 get to feeling decently native on a modern mobile device?

Windows 3.11 runs in a WebAssembly emulator, and the browser rearranges its screen so that it fits,
and works, on a phone. The rule throughout was to keep as much of the work as possible inside the
guest (Windows) and to put little to no HTML or CSS styling in the host (the browser): every pixel
on the page is Windows' own, and the parts that had to be invented were built as native Windows
programs and drivers rather than as web interface.

## How it works

- A custom display driver reports the browser window as the screen. When the window changes shape,
  the display tells Windows, and Windows re-lays-out. This is the inversion the whole thing rests
  on: normally the screen is fixed and the OS picks a mode to fit it.
- The browser cuts Windows' screen into per-window layers and re-stacks them into a single column.
  Each window's contents shrink to fit a phone while its title bar stays finger-sized. Windows is
  never told: as far as it is concerned the windows sit side by side on one very wide screen.
- Touch gestures drive it: tap to click, two fingers to scroll, pinch to magnify, swipe in from the
  right edge to change window, swipe up from the bottom for a card switcher.
- A wide browser window turns all of that off and gives you Windows 3.11 at one guest pixel per
  browser pixel, as it always was.
- Networking is done by the host over a paravirtual socket, so there is no TCP stack inside the
  guest, and a custom Winsock 1.1 makes it available to any period Windows program at over 1 MB/s.
- An optional shader makes the screen look like the passive-matrix LCD panel of a 1992 laptop,
  and it is switched on and off from a Windows control panel inside the guest.

## URLs

The path opens a program. https://win31.gross.is/solitaire opens Solitaire,
/notepad opens Notepad, /jezzball opens JezzBall, and so on; ?run= takes a command line directly.
The full list is in /sitemap.xml.

## Not worth crawling

/image/, /parts/ and /pages/*.pvp are emulator state and binary page bundles.
